extra.message: Attacker-influenced path material reaches a filesystem read/list operation with no basename reduction, resolved-containment check, or allowlist guard.
An uploaded file's bytes are written to storage with no content-type/extension validation in the enclosing handler, allowing a dangerous file type to be persisted and later served.

DELETE /attachments/:id (support_agent/team_lead/admin) finds and deletes any attachment by id (lines 222-246) without the checkTicketAccess used by upload/findByTicket/findById; an agent can delete attachments belonging to tickets/teams outside their scope.

An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: forgotPassword returns the generated reset token in the HTTP response body; a reset credential is disclosed with no filtering or redaction.
Privileged mutation has no durable audit-log record, though this repository's own audit-log convention proves one exists and is reachable.

bcrypt work factor is not a fixed, sufficiently high literal — attacker/config-controlled cost collapses to a fast hash.

POST /escalations (customer_user allowed) uses attacker-controlled dto.ticketId to look up a ticket with no access check, creates an escalation on it (line 101) and flips that ticket's status to escalated (line 122). A customer can escalate and mutate any other org's ticket.

GET /escalations/:id (controller passes client-controlled ?membershipTier). When membershipTier==='partner_reviewer' the service returns the full escalation before the customer_user organization check (line 319-325) runs, so any customer_user can read another org's escalation details by adding the query param — attacker-controlled bypass of the org-binding check.
jwt verify(): algorithms allowlist includes 'none' — attacker-forged unsigned token accepted
jwt verify() failure falls back to jwt.decode() — unverified claims accepted on the failure path
Subprocess spawned with shell:true and a dynamically-built command.

A resource lookup keyed by attacker-variable input branches into two externally distinguishable outcomes: this existence/state check and a second, differently-coded check on the same looked-up entity, letting an attacker probe the identifier to learn a protected state.
Attacker-influenced text reaches a raw line-oriented log sink without control-character neutralization.
Attacker-controlled text is compiled as a server-side template.
Session/token issued (jwt sign) without any expiration.

GET /replies/ticket/:ticketId/suggestion (staff roles) does a findUnique on the untrusted ticketId and returns the ticket's subject+description with no ticket-access check, so any support_agent can exfiltrate other orgs'/teams' ticket content.

GET /reports/ticket/:ticketId/category-summary (support_agent allowed) loads any ticket by untrusted id and returns ticketNumber+subject with no ticket-access check, disclosing cross-org ticket data to any staff member.

Diagnostic/debug detail is disclosed to the client, gated on a caller-controllable request field (query/header/cookie/body) rather than a server-side environment or deployment check: if (opsContext === 'internal-ops') {

GET /tickets findAll: for support_agent/team_lead no tenant/queue where-clause is applied (lines 219-227 are a no-op), and attacker-controlled filters.organizationId is applied verbatim (line 244). Any agent can list all tickets across every organization (mass cross-tenant exposure), contradicting the intended team-scoped access.

GET /tickets/:id/replies uses checkSimpleAccess, which only enforces the org check for customer_user; support_agent/team_lead are unrestricted, so they can read reply threads of any org's/team's tickets despite the intended assignee/team binding.

GET /tickets/:id/internal-notes is staff-role-gated only (line 893) but never binds the attacker-supplied ticketId to the caller's org/team/assignee (unlike checkTicketAccess used by findById/update). Any support_agent/team_lead can read internal notes of any ticket in any organization.

GET /tickets/:id/timeline uses checkSimpleAccess, which only restricts customer_user by org; for staff no predicate binds the ticketId to the caller's team/queue. Any authenticated staff can fetch the full timeline of any org's ticket including internal notes and audit logs.
